It supplies per-row `product`, `relative_path`, `image_sha256` and `targets`, so labels and filenames can be attached to panel ordinals.\n\nMy `find` for local mirrors timed out at 60 s, so that check is inconclusive.\n\n## Score semantics (from `packed_quality`)\n\n- **Row layout:** per row, 128 signed int8 codes, then a little-endian float16 inverse norm (`struct 'e'`).\n- **Score:** `f32( f32(dot \u00b7 inv_q) \u00b7 inv_g )`. The integer dot is exact in float32, since its maximum is about 2.06M, below 2\u00b2\u2074. Emulate the two roundings with a `struct 'f'` round-trip.\n- **Ranking:** stable descending sort over the gallery; ties go to the lower gallery position.\n- **Metrics:** R1 is the top-1 match. AP is AP@R, with R_q the number of same-product gallery items, normalised by R_q.\n- **Roles:** query and gallery are disjoint, so the score is Q\u2192G only.\n\n## CPU bound (estimate, not benchmarked)\n\n- Each endpoint needs 1734 \u00d7 1715 = 2.97M dots of length 128, which is 380.6M multiply-adds.\n- With `sum(map(mul,a,b))` I'd expect about 30 s per endpoint and about 3 min for all 6. Memory should stay under 100 MB on one core, well inside the receipt's 700 s / 8 GiB CPU policy.\n\n## What the receipt alone already gives (index level, no new reads)\n\nR1-error counts per endpoint, by query-order index:\n\n| Endpoint | Errors |\n|---|---|\n| control 179061 / 179069 | 56 / 57 |\n| candidate 179061 / 179069 | 50 / 51 |\n| source | 64 |\n| concat | 61 |\n\n- 44 queries are wrong in all four connected endpoints, 39 if source and concat are included, and 64 are wrong in at least one.\n- Candidate-vs-control R1 flips are small: 0\u21921 is 11 and 12, 1\u21920 is 5 and 6, net +6 each seed. The paired R1 interval is [\u22120.00085, +0.0083], which spans zero. The KILL rests on `quality_pass=False` and `product_go=False`.\n\n## Are the same-view and mutual-confusion inferences justified?\n\n**Same-view filenames: not justified yet.**\n- The receipt pins 3449 selection image paths, but not their order.\n  - The paths for the 498 selection products can be recovered from `input_guards`, and they total exactly 3449.\n  - The panel-ordinal \u2194 path mapping cannot be recovered locally. I tried two plausible fit-row orders (sorted path; product-id-major then path). Both fail: 829 and 936 products span several panel roles, and the selection product sets and the diagnostic's query counts don't match.\n- Even with `fit.json`, a filename view tag only counts as evidence against two comparators:\n  - **Chance rate:** over the 3449 selection images the tags are front 837, side 726, back 698, additional 682, full 448, flat 58, so chance same-tag is 0.20.\n  - **Correct top-1 hits:** embeddings encode pose strongly, so the same-view rate among wrong top-1 matches must be compared with the rate among correct ones.\n\n**Mutual confusion and label noise: not supported.**\n- Q and G are disjoint, so \"mutual\" is a new statistic and needs an explicit definition, for example product-level A\u2192B and B\u2192A on core errors with a degree-preserving null.\n- Mutual near-neighbour pairs are also expected under correct labels, because In-Shop colorways of one style are separate `id_` products.\n- The only label-noise test the receipt supports is exact duplicates: all 16,456 guarded files have distinct sha256, so there are no byte-identical images across products. Near-duplicates are untested.\n- I would not endorse a label-noise claim, or any Knear\u22658 trigger. There is no preregistered distribution behind it. Choosing a threshold on 44 core errors in an already-exposed panel is post-hoc, and it can't explain a mAP gain that comes from 381 positive-AP queries.\n\n## Plan\n\n1. The root approves one read-only copy of the four `packed.bin` files (plus optional baselines) and `fit.json`. Check every file against its receipt sha before use.\n2. Write one stdlib script, a descriptive census only, that reuses the semantics above.\n3. **Falsifying admission gate:** the recompute must match the receipt's `per_query_r1` exactly and `per_query_ap` within 1e-6 on all 4 endpoints (and source/concat). Output per-query fields: top-1 gallery ordinal and product, wrong-top-1 score, best-positive rank and margin, R_q, AP. No threshold, trigger or arm admission comes from it.\n\n## Risks\n\n- The census only describes a panel that was already exposed. It can't reopen KILL, and any threshold derived from it is post-hoc.\n- One product, `id_00003523`, has 162 selection images (81 queries), about 4.7% of the queries, and its R=81 AP@R weight is large. Report per-product contributions so it doesn't drive the result.\n- The wire files may no longer be on the remote disk.",
